1	// Room "P3 kitchen" (interior designer's part): the kitchen is 3 x 2 cells (x58..60, z19..20), feet at y2. The front
2	// door (59,18) and the back door (58,21) both open onto a clear first cell, so (59,19) and (58,20) stay bare, and the
3	// only lane between them runs through (59,20). The stove runs down the east wall under the window pair, its fronts
4	// facing west into the room (the focal piece, both lit). The barrel counter sits on the west wall with a potted poppy
5	// on its lid. Nothing hangs over the doorways.
6	import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";
7	
8	export function build(g) {
9	  const legend = {
10	    // feet level: x58 z19 is the barrel counter, x60 z19..20 the stove (smoker north, furnace south)
11	    "B": ["barrel", { facing: "up", open: "true" }],
12	    "S": ["smoker", { facing: "west", lit: "true" }],
13	    "F": ["furnace", { facing: "west", lit: "true" }],
14	    // the potted flower stands on the barrel lid (y3)
15	    "P": ["potted_poppy", {}],
16	    // a lantern hangs from the ceiling over the barrel counter (y4), the tool's lamp spot
17	    "L": ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }],
18	  };
19	  // rows run along +x (58, 59, 60), successive rows along +z (19, 20); layer y2, then y3, then y4
20	  layers(g, [58, 2, 19], legend, [
21	    ["B.S", "..F"],
22	    ["P..", "..."],
23	    ["L..", "..."],
24	  ]);
25	}

input.summary:
P3 kitchen (room-25.mjs) now builds clean: make.sh exits 0, writes build.nbt, and its line shows no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE.
The part is now empty: the stove, barrel counter, potted poppy and lantern were removed, and the intended layout is kept as a comment in the file.
Cause: shell west already wrote air into every kitchen cell (x58..60, y2..4, z19..20), and runParts locks air as well as solid blocks, so no room part can place furniture there.

waste.what: Finding which earlier part owned each kitchen cell: I had to run the build with MCD_PARTS_CELLS and write a throwaway node script to map cells to owning parts, one cell at a time.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and one probe script; 18 cells checked
waste.tool: runParts should report the owning part and say that air counts as owned (for example 'x58 y2 z19 owned by shell west=air'). An `mcd` command that lists the free cells of a room box would show at once that the room has none.

waste.what: Reading the refusal wording: REFUSED reports only the block that was wanted and the block that was there ('air'), so 'air' looked like a free cell when it was locked.
waste.cost: one extra read of build.mjs runParts to confirm the lock covers air
waste.tool: The REFUSED line should say 'locked air' or name the owning part, so a designer doesn't try to move writes into another locked air cell.

waste.what: Off-palette checks run only after the lock check, so refused blocks are never palette-checked. I checked barrel, smoker, furnace, potted_poppy and lantern against palette.json by hand.
waste.tool: runParts could palette-check every attempted write, refused or not, so a refused part still reports its off-palette blocks.

companions.task: Place the smoker, furnace, barrel counter and potted poppy in the kitchen once the shell leaves those cells free or the lock lets the room fit out its own air.
Hang the lantern over the barrel counter at y4 and confirm the kitchen has no dark cell, once the fit-out can be placed.

left: The kitchen furniture is not built: the smoker, furnace, barrel counter, potted poppy and lantern were removed to clear the REFUSED report, so the room is an empty box. This needs the shell-west part to leave x58..60, y2..4, z19..20 unbuilt, or runParts to allow a room to fit out air that the shell carved. Neither is in parts/room-25.mjs, so I did not change them.
The layout is kept as a comment in parts/room-25.mjs so it can be restored with the same coordinates and states.
The lock blocks every room part, not just this one: any interior furniture in a room whose cells the shell wrote as air will be refused the same way.
